pages.title: Solar Leasing Companies in California: How to Compare Them
pages.note: What a leasing company is (EPA roles; contracts sold to investors per Sunrun 10-K), California ownership mix from CPUC-authorized DG Stats (2025: 54.5% owned, 41.7% PPA, 3.1% lease; 2026 YTD 58.7/35.1/4.6), the 2025 tax law's new 26 USC 48E(i) (no business credit on leased residential solar, taxable years beginning after 2025-07-04; PPAs not named), a CPUC-sourced comparison checklist, one provider's 10-K contract terms as a benchmark (not a recommendation), Sunnova Chapter 11 as the failure example. No ranking. Lease cost-per-month questions answered by linking the existing cost and rent pages rather than repeating them. Partial only because the holder link from /solar-companies/los-angeles is requested, not made (not owned).

pages.title: Solar PPA Companies in California: How to Compare Offers
pages.note: Kept distinct from the leasing page: PPA definition (CPUC, EPA four-party model), PPA share in California (DG Stats), the 48E(e)(4) solar cutoff (placed in service after 2027-12-31 for construction starting after 2026-07-04) and why a 2026-27 PPA price may depend on it, a 7-point comparison list (price per kWh test linked to the hub's #ppa-price-per-kwh), prepaid shortfall refunds and end-of-term options as one provider's 10-K terms, provider failure. Answers 'can you buy out a solar ppa' and 'what is a prepaid ppa' by linking. Partial only for the holder link request (/solar-companies/los-angeles).

pages.title: 10 kW Solar System Cost in California: What 2025 Data Shows
pages.note: Cost basis is California DG Stats (CPUC-authorized per D.14-11-001), residential solar-only average cost per AC watt for systems >=10 kW, 2025 permission-to-operate year, pulled from the site's own chart endpoint (/api/v1.2/interconnection/cpw_over_time, sector=res, basis=nominal): all IOUs $4.26 (n=3,966), PG&E $4.08 (2,173), SCE $3.42 (664), SDG&E $5.11 (1,129); 2026 YTD $4.35 (772). Dollar figures for 10 kW are labeled as our arithmetic. Berkeley Lab 2026 update for installer spread ($2.4-$6.3/W medians), size distribution, storage premium (+$2.1/W) and loan premium, all quoted from its text. No production figure: NREL's PVWatts API was blocked by the proxy, so the page links PVWatts instead. Partial only because the CREATE_DEDICATED holder (/commercial-solar/cost-per-watt-california, commercial lane) needs the link; requested.
